source.publisher: National Crime Agency (NECC) / HM Treasury OFSI / JMLIT
source.title: Financial Sanctions Evasion Typologies: Russian Elites and Enablers (Red Alert 0697-NECC)

summary: A UK NECC/OFSI/JMLIT Red Alert (July 2022, ref 0697-NECC) warns that Russian designated persons (DPs) and their London-based professional enablers are evading UK financial sanctions by transferring shareholdings to trusted proxies, divesting stakes below the 50% control threshold, and using nominee directors, trust structures and complex offshore corporate arrangements to disguise continued control of frozen assets. It notes exploitation of differing designation timescales across the UK, US and EU, use of secrecy jurisdictions, alternative payment channels including crypto-assets to bypass SWIFT restrictions, and pooled accounts and off-the-shelf shell corporations used by TCSPs and other enablers as throughputs. It lists 34 detection indicators across frozen-asset transfers, enabler activity and suspicious payments, and sets out reporting routes to OFSI and NCA SARs, plus responses from the NCA's Combating Kleptocracy Cell and professional body supervisors.

citations.quote: Transfer assets such as shareholdings in holding companies to trusted proxies such as relatives or employees;
Changes to ownership of a corporate holding to reduce ownership stakes to below the 50% threshold, shortly before or after sanctions designations.

Use of trust arrangements or complex corporate structures involving offshore companies, with circumstances of transfers calling into question whether the original owner retains indirect control or otherwise could retain a benefit from the assets transferred.
Russian money launderers have increasingly been observed in UK intelligence and operational activity providing cash to crypto-asset services, with the ability to move significant volumes of funds.
Circumvention attempts through Open Account Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML) typology, such as increases in third party open account payments.
A large number of off-the-shelf corporations with no trading record with nominee ownership used as throughputs.

Numerous transfers of shares from sanctioned entities to non-sanctioned entities involving corporations incorporated by the same people and company (often with a registered office at the same physical address).

typologies.label: High Risk Jurisdictions

citations.quote: Holding companies based in jurisdictions that are offshore and/or historically linked to former Soviet Union (excluding Baltics and Ukraine) jurisdictions.
Holding companies based in jurisdictions that are offshore a nd/or historically linked to ass ets in the former Soviet Union.
Identification of transactions by holding companies linked with DPs with Swiss bank accounts and BVI / Cypriot legal persons.

Payments via a Fintech with Russian investor nexus including customer’s transactions that are initiated from or sent to IP addresses that have non-trusted sources, or are located in Russia, Belarus, jurisdictions with FATF-identified AML deficiencies or comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Indicators 11, 28, 29, 32 in the 'Indicators' section (frozen asset transfers and suspicious payments sub-sections), pages 10-12. SAN008 doctrine: 'High-Risk-Jurisdiction exposure measures how much of an entity's footprint... touches sanctioned, embargoed or high-risk jurisdictions... the jurisdiction is not an aggravating detail behind another finding; it *is* the finding.' The advisory's suspicious-payments indicator set flags holding companies and payment counterparties purely on jurisdictional grounds -- offshore/former-Soviet registration, Swiss/BVI/Cypriot legal persons, and Fintech payments routed to/from Russia, Belarus, FATF-deficient or comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions -- without requiring a resolved ownership chain or trade mismatch. That is exactly SAN008's stand-alone jurisdiction-as-finding mechanism, and it is developed across four separate bullets, not a single passing mention.

typologies.label: Front Companies

citations.quote: Numerous transfers of shares from sanctioned entities to non-sanctioned entities involving corporations incorporated by the same people and company (often with a registered office at the same physical address).
A large number of off-the-shelf corporations with no trading record with nominee ownership used as throughputs.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Indicators 20-21, 'For detection of enablers' sub-section, page 11. SAN004 doctrine: 'A front company is an entity with little or no genuine economic substance, established to give a sanctioned interest a clean commercial face. It exists to transact -- to hold accounts, sign contracts and move goods -- while the real party stays hidden behind it.' Indicator 21 describes exactly this: off-the-shelf corporations with no trading record and nominee ownership used purely as 'throughputs', and indicator 20 shows them absorbing share transfers from sanctioned entities. The entities have no substance of their own and exist solely to move the sanctioned interest's value onward, matching SAN004's mechanism rather than the broader shell-network pattern-matching already claimed under PAT007.

typologies.label: Third Party Payment Abuse

citations.quote: Circumvention attempts through Open Account Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML) typology, such as increases in third party open account payments.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Indicator 34, 'For detection of suspicious payments' sub-section, page 12. TBML008 doctrine: 'Third Party Payment Abuse settles a trade through a payer who is not the trade counterparty... The payment breaks the link between the trade and the funds.' Indicator 34 names this mechanism almost verbatim -- 'increases in third party open account payments' as a sanctions-circumvention technique -- describing settlement of an open-account trade by a payer outside the trade relationship, which is precisely TBML008's payer/counterparty mismatch, not the goods- or invoice-based mechanism already claimed under TBML010.

typologies.label: Citizenship-by-Investment Nationality Laundering

citations.quote: Change of UBOs from Russian nationals to persons of other nationalities, potentially with names of Russian origin but from third-country jurisdictions (including, but not limited to, countries that offer citizenship-by-investment schemes).
Investor visa or golden passport holders changing ownership information or divesting investments.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Indicators 12-13, 'For detection of frozen asset transfers' sub-section, pages 10-11. No existing typology covers nationality substitution via citizenship-by-investment/golden-passport programmes as the evasion mechanism itself (searched 'citizenship by investment / golden passport' and 'name screening evasion' -- best score 0.44 on an unrelated network-workflow typology). SAN001 Ownership Evasion's mechanism is layered holding structures and nominee arrangements; SAN005 Name Screening Evasion's mechanism is engineering the *form* of a name (aliases, transliterations) to defeat exact-match filters. Here the DP's associate instead acquires a genuinely new, different nationality and passport through an investment scheme, so the underlying identity itself changes rather than the ownership chain or the name's spelling -- a distinct technique the two related bullets develop together.

typologies.label: Enabler Pooled Account Screening Concealment

citations.quote: Pooled accounts, in which banks see only the name of the enabler and not the client , transferring funds to entities associated in open source with DPs.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Indicator 18, 'For detection of enablers' sub-section, page 11. No matching doctrine was found (search for 'pooled/omnibus account concealing underlying client identity' returned nothing above noise). BA002 Funnel Accounts' mechanism is many dispersed depositors clearing to one beneficiary fast -- a volume/dispersion tell; BA009 Transaction Laundering's mechanism runs through card-processing rails. Neither matches this indicator's mechanism, which is that the bank's own name-screening never sees the true client at all because the enabler's name sits on the account -- a screening-blind-spot technique distinct from both. Single-bullet evidence, hence low confidence.

extraction_notes: Document is a UK NCA/OFSI Red Alert combining narrative context (pp.3-9) with a numbered indicator list (34 items, pp.10-12); typology confidence reflects how developed each theme is, not just presence. SAN001 (Ownership Evasion) is the dominant, well-developed theme (high confidence). SAN009, CMI010, TBML010 and PAT007 rest on fewer, more narrowly stated passages and are scored medium/low accordingly. The document also references transfers to "the former Soviet Union (excluding the Baltic States and Ukraine)" as a destination for evasion, which could not be mapped to specific ISO codes and is omitted from the jurisdictions list. Enablers and DPs are recorded as category-type actors per instruction, since the document describes classes of actors rather than named individuals/organisations. No named individual or corporate actor is identified in the text supplied. Merged 5 reviewer addition(s) under schema 1.4.0; each carries its review_justification. Extraction-only record retained at data/records/.
